judgment.reasoning_summary: The polynomial P(x) = x^n - 5x + 4 must have all integer roots. By the Rational Root Theorem, any integer root must be a divisor of the constant term, which is 4. The possible integer roots are therefore ±1, ±2, and ±4. We need to check if these values can be roots for different values of n. For n = 1, P(x) = x - 5x + 4 = -4x + 4, which has no integer roots. For n = 2, P(x) = x^2 - 5x + 4, which factors as (x - 1)(x - 4), so the roots are 1 and 4. For n = 3, P(x) = x^3 - 5x + 4, which does not factor nicely and has no integer roots. For n = 4, P(x) = x^4 - 5x + 4, which also does not factor nicely and has no integer roots. For n > 4, the polynomial will have higher degree terms that prevent it from having all integer roots. Therefore, the only value of n for which P(x) has all integer roots is n = 2.
